title: Finite relative marked saturation and perfectness
statement:
Use the marked objects, arbitrary-base cartesian fibrations, natural markings and relative sharp mapping complexes in [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus]. For any small simplicial set $S$, let $W_S$ consist of marked maps $f:U	o V$ over $S$ for which restriction $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(V,Z^
atural)	o\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(U,Z^
atural)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every small cartesian fibration $Z	o S$. A class of arrows is perfect here if it contains isomorphisms, satisfies two-out-of-three, is closed under filtered colimits in the arrow category, and every one of its arrows is a filtered colimit of arrows in a fixed small subset of that class.

Assume that for every map $g:P^
atural	o Q^
atural$ of naturally marked cartesian fibrations over $S$, membership $g\in W_S$ is equivalent to every vertex-fiber map $g_s:P_s	o Q_s$ being an equivalence of quasicategories. There is a functor $T_S$ on marked objects over $S$, with natural map $\eta_U:U	o T_S(U)$, such that $T_S(U)=Q_U^
atural$ for a cartesian fibration $Q_U	o S$, every $\eta_U$ belongs to $W_S$, and $T_S$ preserves filtered colimits. One may take $T_S$ to be the sequential finite-cell saturation obtained by adjoining fillers over $S$ for the finite generators (i), (ii), (iii) and $A^ lat	o A$ of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], with $A$ the finite equivalence-edge detector defined there; the maps of types (i), (ii), (iii) are given every possible base map, while each detector $A^ lat	o A$ is labelled by a constant map to a vertex of $S$. The class $W_S$ is perfect. These assertions are about the explicit mapping-test class, without presupposing a model structure on marked objects over $S$, and all objects and sets in them can be formed in the input universe.
